title: The Detective Boys Become Models
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0912.txt (389 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Detective Takagi, Detective Sato, Inspector Megure, and the rest of the Detective Boys) omitted by convention -- they function only as the alibi-verification mechanism (modeling for Nishiyama's painting, then investigating), not as suspects/victims/motive-holders in the underlying crime. The old low-fidelity cases/ file's culprit (Daiki Nishiyama, here p5) is CONFIRMED CORRECT by the transcript -- he confesses outright at the end -- so no culprit reversal was needed here, unlike several other rebuilds. What the old file got wrong/thin: (1) its has_motive_against edge for the culprit was 'unspecified (not stated in the available source excerpt)', but the transcript states the motive directly and early, via Kinuko's accusation later confirmed true in Nishiyama's own confession -- Seiho extorted money from artists in exchange for selecting their pieces as exhibition winners, and Nishiyama couldn't afford to pay, so his work kept losing; (2) it collapsed all alibi-checking into one generic 'was_at' edge per suspect at a single studio location, when the transcript actually tracks four distinct, individually-checked alibi claims (Higashio: home all day, actually with a married woman; Kinuko: department-store shopping, actually at a host club; Shizu: supermarket run, confirmed; Nishiyama: painting at Lake Okuho + a real train-departure-sign photo) across five named locations; (3) it never modeled the actual train-schedule/departure-sign timing trick that breaks Nishiyama's alibi (the departure sign advances on a fixed schedule rather than on the train's real departure, discovered by revisiting Aohata Station, which is what lets the vandalized crossing-gate delay put Nishiyama on an earlier train than his photo implies); (4) the accusatory red herrings against Higashio and Kinuko are added here as has_motive_against edges tagged red_herring, matching the ep011 pattern, since the old file had no motive edges for them at all. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: The alibi painting's background shows the felled tree still under barricade tape from a job finished the week before, but that tape/tree were long gone by the murder day -- proving the landscape layer was painted earlier than claimed.

Revisiting Aohata Station shows its departure sign switching to the next train before the delayed train had actually left, proving the sign timing (as seen in Nishiyama's alibi photo) does not verify which physical train he boarded -- tying the vandalized crossing-gate delay directly to his opportunity window.
